commitResults.messageTitle: Update the initial code to simply greet the user and exit.
Handled errors, refactored code and added delete feature
Add task loading with structured file persistence
Handle corrupted task data and storage error
Extract task list management into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Encapsulate task collection operations behind a dedicated TaskList class while preserving Friday's command flow, storage behavior, and console output. Keep Friday responsible for orchestration and expose only a read-only view for persistence and display.

Move task-file path management, loading, saving, record parsing, date reconstruction, escaping, and corruption warnings out of Friday. Keep Friday responsible for coordinating the session and presenting storage warnings while preserving existing behavior.

Move command classification, task creation, date parsing, validation, and task-number parsing out of Friday. Keep Friday focused on executing typed commands and preserving the existing console behavior.

Move command input and all user-facing output from Friday into Ui, leaving Friday responsible for coordinating parsing, task updates, storage, and error flow while preserving existing console transcripts.

Replace Parser's tagged command record with an abstract Command hierarchy for add, delete, exit, list, mark, and unmark operations. Each command owns its task mutation and UI response, while Friday coordinates parsing, guarded persistence, and loop termination.
Merge the Ui extraction and executable command hierarchy into master, preserving the refactored application coordination structure.

Move the application, command, model, parser, storage, UI, and exception classes beneath the friday package hierarchy while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Update the UI test runner for recursive compilation and the packaged entry point, and refresh the README path.
Merge the package hierarchy, packaged application entry point, and recursive UI test support into master.
Point the Gradle application plugin at friday.Friday, the packaged chatbot entry point, so Gradle run tasks launch the current application.
Merge Gradle build support and the corrected packaged application entry point into master.
Cover successful task removal, order preservation, returned values, and invalid-index behavior for empty and non-empty lists.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand JUnit coverage for core logic
commitResults.messageBody: Cover all public TaskList operations and boundary behavior, command parsing and validation, and storage round trips, missing files, and corrupted records. These tests target the highest-value business logic and raise automated coverage across the core classes.
Set the approximate 50 percent high-value method coverage target and require updating or adding JUnit tests after each code change, followed by running the Gradle test suite.
Merge the high-value JUnit coverage and documented 50 percent testing target into master.
Configure the Shadow plugin to produce friday-all.jar with friday.Friday as its manifest entry point, include the artifact in the build lifecycle, and document how to create and run it.
Merge executable Shadow JAR configuration and usage documentation into master.

Add stretch-level Javadocs to all non-private production classes and methods, non-trivial helpers, constructors, and JUnit test methods. Clarify task, command, parser, storage, UI, and exception contracts without changing behavior.
Merge comprehensive JavaDoc documentation for production APIs and JUnit tests into master.

Java sources lack a project-local reference for SE-EDU conventions, and Git guidance is not encoded in the agent instructions.

Add project-specific Java and Git skills, then require them through AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md so future edits and commits follow consistent rules.

Align existing Java imports and class declarations with the coding standard without changing runtime behavior.

Friday cannot currently narrow the task list by description, so users must inspect every task manually.

Add a find command that performs case-insensitive substring matching and displays matching tasks in list order. Reject empty keywords and show a clear no-match message.

Cover parser and TaskList behavior with JUnit tests and add a UI transcript using persisted initial data.
Configure Gradle to run Checkstyle with the project coding standard. Fix existing formatting violations in storage parsing and parser tests so the new checks pass consistently.

Introduce the JavaFX bootstrap, FXML views, controller, and reusable dialog control for the chatbot.

Reuse the existing parser and command model through a JavaFX-independent
Chatbot adapter, while preserving the console application behavior.

Add standardized Tony Stark and F.R.I.D.A.Y. avatar resources and coverage
for chatbot responses.
Integrate the JavaFX chatbot interface, FXML views, reusable dialog controls, and standardized avatar resources into the main branch.

Allow callers to create a task list from individual task arguments while preserving the existing List-based constructor for storage loading.

Test the new constructor to ensure task order is retained.
Add a varargs TaskList constructor for convenient creation from individual tasks while retaining list-based loading support.

Friday's main control flow relies on several internal objects and method
contracts being non-null, but those assumptions are implicit.

Implicit assumptions make unexpected control-flow or contract violations
harder to identify during development and maintenance.

Add Java assertions at the storage-load, command-loop, parser, and task-saving
boundaries to document these invariants and fail close to the source of a
violation. Keep input validation and recoverable storage errors in the
existing exception-handling flow.
Document runtime assumptions with assertions

Friday's main method combines application setup, saved-task recovery, command
processing, and shutdown in one method that is longer than the recommended
readable size.

Keeping these responsibilities together makes the main control flow harder to
scan and forces readers to understand implementation details before seeing the
overall session structure.

Extract session loading and command processing into focused private methods.
Keep the existing behavior and assertions in their relevant parts of the
session lifecycle so each method has one clear responsibility.

Storage.save builds the list of persisted task lines by manually creating a
list and appending one serialized task at a time.

The loop obscures that this operation is a direct transformation from tasks to
their file representations and adds mutable accumulation that the operation
does not need.

Use a stream to map each task to its file representation and collect the
results into a list. Preserve the original task order and serialized output
while expressing the transformation more directly.
Shorten Friday session coordinator
Branch a streams

Friday only stores active tasks, so users cannot set tasks aside without
deleting their record permanently.

Add commands to archive one or all active tasks, display archived tasks, and
restore one or all archived tasks. Persist the archive separately while
preserving the existing task-file format and task ordering.

Update parser, console output, tests, UI transcripts, and user documentation.
Keep archive commands console-only because the JavaFX chatbot has no persistent
storage session.
Add task archiving commands

Replace mirrored chat rows with responsive assistant and user message styles, and make validation errors visually distinct. Add compact circular participant images, a stylesheet, and UI design notes so the application is easier to scan while preserving message space.
Polish FRIDAY chat interface
Show the supplied FRIDAY profile image in the header, use the requested welcome message, and define the send icon in FXML so it renders reliably in JavaFX.
Refine FRIDAY window header

Align console and JavaFX responses with FRIDAY's composed assistant identity through deterministic greetings, concise acknowledgements, and clear complication wording. Update the GUI palette and transcript documentation to match the new voice.
Give FRIDAY a distinctive personality

Handle null, blank, padded, and repeated-whitespace input without crashes; reject invalid task numbers and event ranges; and prevent duplicate task details. Make storage access failures explicit and skip duplicate or chronologically invalid records while preserving valid data.
Harden command and data validation

Replace the placeholder guide with a GitHub-Flavored Markdown reference covering setup, GUI and console usage, commands, archive behavior, error handling, persistence, personality, and troubleshooting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JavaFX dependencies for all platforms
commitResults.messageBody:
The Shadow JAR previously included JavaFX native libraries only for the platform used to build it, which prevented the packaged application from supporting the other operating systems.

Declare the base, controls, FXML, and graphics JavaFX artifacts for Windows, macOS, and Linux so Gradle packages the platform libraries required by the course's cross-platform JAR workflow.

Core task types and command behaviors were not covered comprehensively, leaving serialization, status transitions, duplicate detection, and command responses vulnerable to regressions.

Add focused JUnit tests for common task behavior, todo/deadline/event formatting and equality, command success paths, validation failures, and list/find/exit responses. Keep GUI rendering outside the automated suite because it requires manual cross-platform verification.

Integrate expanded automated coverage for the core task and command layers.

The new tests cover task serialization and status behavior, concrete task formatting and equality, command success paths, validation failures, duplicate detection, and user-facing responses. Keep GUI rendering outside this suite because it requires manual platform-specific checks.
